clue.text: One getting post at residential address?

definitions.text: One getting post at residential address?

parts.words: One getting post at residential address?
parts.note: reads like someone receiving letters at their house, but 'post' is a job: this person's employment is carried on where they live

explanation.surface: Someone receiving letters delivered to their house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' suggests mail; here it means a position of employment, and the residential address is where the work is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who works from their own house takes up a job based at their residence.

clue.text: Architectural moulding is old — gosh!

parts.note: gee is an exclamation like gosh

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at an antique piece of decorative moulding.
explanation.definitionFit: An S-shaped curved moulding or arch found in buildings.

clue.text: Learner is entering part of hospital to sign up

indicators.note: going into, so these pieces sit inside the hospital department

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
L is a learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A trainee goes into a hospital ward to register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts L and IS inside ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To join the armed forces or volunteer for a cause.

clue.text: Mountains around which you'll find very large fruit trees

indicators.note: says the mountains have the size letters placed around them

parts.note: OS is outsize, a clothing size
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: Big fruit trees grow on the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around which you'll find' wraps O...S around RANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Citrus trees grown for their fruit, as in an orchard of Seville.

clue.text: Powder that sounds like something black (and it is)

indicators.note: signals a word that is said the same as the answer

parts.note: coal is proverbially black

explanation.surface: A cosmetic powder named after something dark, and dark itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket points out that the powder itself is black too.
explanation.definitionFit: A black eye cosmetic powder, used for lining the eyes.

clue.text: King — confused, old and debauched

parts.note: R is rex, Latin for king
addled means muddled or confused

explanation.surface: A monarch, muddled, aged and dissipated.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing signs of age and hard living, worn out by dissipation.

clue.text: Instrument offering a succession of musical pieces in just one key?

parts.note: a concert is a programme of music
taken as written
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: A recital where every piece is in the same key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just one key' is the key of A.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hexagonal bellows-and-button squeezebox.

clue.text: Get offhand in journey — there's only a little illumination

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a flight is a journey by air
airy means casual or offhand

explanation.surface: Someone acts casually on a trip where the lighting is dim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' is just a link; 'in' places AIRY inside FLIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny decorative bulb, as on a Christmas tree, gives only a faint glow.

clue.text: Some Cypriot admiring Greek character

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Cypriot admires a figure from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth letter of the Greek alphabet is a character of that script.

clue.text: When in trouble, he called by and went on complaining

indicators.note: being in trouble suggests things in disorder, so the following letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man in difficulty dropped by and kept grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges HE CALLED BY; 'When' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To grouse at length is informally to moan as if with a stomach pain, a slang verb for whining.

clue.text: Man about to meet the queen — an entertainer

parts.note: Dan is a man's name
C is short for circa, Latin for about
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: A man is about to have an audience with the queen, a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballet or stage performer who moves to music is one kind of entertainer.

clue.text: Please repair the pier

indicators.note: to repair is to fix up and rebuild, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A request to mend the seaside jetty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repair' rearranges THE PIER into an archaic word for 'please'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned contraction of 'I pray thee', used as a polite request.

clue.text: One can get off to a fast start, despite what the crossword compiler says!

definitions.text: One can get off to a fast start

parts.note: pace, Latin, means with respect to, used when disagreeing with someone
a setter compiles crosswords

explanation.surface: A runner may sprint off quickly, whatever the puzzler claims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pace X' means 'with due respect to X, who would disagree'.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who leads to set the speed for a race starts off quickly.

clue.text: Given the situation, the satanic must be destroyed

indicators.note: destroying the words breaks them up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A call to wipe out all things devilish.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning 'if so' or 'under those circumstances'.

clue.text: About to spin having absorbed the anaesthetic?

indicators.note: taking in, so one piece is placed inside the other
spinning turns the word round so it reads backwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone about to go into a spin after drinking a sedative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to spin' turns RE into ER; 'having absorbed' puts THE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A volatile liquid once widely used to put patients to sleep for surgery.

clue.text: Sarah has always hugged quite a few!

indicators.note: something hugged is held in the arms, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Sal is a pet form of Sarah
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: Sarah has given a good many people a cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning more than two but not many, a synonym for a handful or more.

clue.text: Prophet without name to show contempt

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, so the prophet surrounds the letter

parts.note: a seer is a prophet

explanation.surface: An anonymous prophet curls the lip.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff or smirk derisively.

clue.text: Good person also gets to suffer

parts.note: ST abbreviates saint, a good person
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A virtuous individual also ends up suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up with or tolerate, as in 'I can't bear it'.

clue.text: Clever blow delivered with energy

parts.note: a cut is a stroke or blow, as with a sword
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A smart punch thrown with vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd or sharp-witted, a sense of the word beside 'sweet'.

clue.text: Heather has brief affair — fellow goes off

indicators.note: the fellow leaves, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: a fling is a short romance

explanation.surface: A woman called Heather has a quick romance and her man walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for common heather, the moorland shrub Calluna.

clue.text: Surrounded plant receiving little sun

indicators.note: the plant takes in the other piece, which sits inside it

parts.note: beet is a plant grown for its root
S is short for sun

explanation.surface: A hemmed-in plant gets only a little sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemmed in or besieged on all sides, as by enemies or troubles.

clue.text: Sort of advantage the clergy may have

definitions.text: Sort of advantage the clergy may have

parts.words: Sort of advantage the clergy may have
parts.note: refers to the historical legal privilege by which clergy could claim trial in church rather than secular courts

explanation.surface: A perk enjoyed by priests.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase completes '... of clergy', a medieval legal privilege.
explanation.definitionFit: An advantage or perk, here the one named in the old phrase about clergy's legal immunity.

clue.text: Rag covers worn fabric

indicators.note: the rag wraps around the other piece

parts.note: tat is rags or shabby stuff
bare means threadbare, worn

explanation.surface: A rag hides threadbare cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rag' looks like a verb; it is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A stout silk upholstery material with satin stripes.

clue.text: Church composer, one to add colour

definitions.meaning: Sir John ..., Victorian organist and composer of church music
a person or thing that dyes or tints

explanation.surface: A hymn writer who also brightens things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John wrote The Crucifixion; as a common noun the word is a dyer or tinter.

clue.text: Batterer to divide defensive structure

parts.note: a ram is used to batter down gates
to part is to divide or separate

explanation.surface: A battering device is meant to split a fortification.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthen bank or wall around a fort, built for protection.

clue.text: Out of date? Right — but not a failer!

parts.note: passé means old-fashioned

explanation.surface: An outdated idea is correct, yet not a flop.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who succeeds in an exam, the opposite of one who fails.

clue.text: Seize rubbish stuff supplied by the French

parts.note: tack is informal for cheap, tasteless goods, as in 'tacky'
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Grab cheap goods sold by the French.
explanation.definitionFit: To grab or bring down an opponent, as in rugby.

clue.text: Game in the water …

definitions.meaning: a cue sport played on a table with pockets
a small body of still water

explanation.surface: Playing sport while swimming.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a cue game like billiards and a pond or swimming bath.

clue.text: … It's that and nothing more

definitions.meaning: 'that' refers back to the previous clue's watery answer, a small lake

explanation.surface: A continuation saying it is just a pond, no more.
explanation.definitionFit: A lake or pond, and an adjective meaning 'just' or 'only'.

clue.text: Was in full vigour in meal, then I dropped

parts.note: flour is ground meal
shed means dropped or cast off

explanation.surface: Someone was going strong at dinner, then collapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrive or prosper is to bloom, at the height of one's powers.

clue.text: Irish poetry — first volume is missing

indicators.note: missing means taken away, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: verse is poetry

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word volume

explanation.surface: An Irish book of verse lacks its first volume.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gaelic language of Ireland, an old name for Irish.

clue.text: Plan Christmas dinner and have a frank discussion

definitions.meaning: literally, discuss the festive roast bird
idiom for speaking plainly about business

explanation.surface: Organise the festive meal and speak plainly.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally it is chat about the festive bird; as an idiom it means to get down to plain business.
